To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) ‘Lucky’ (opportunistic, agency-prone) CEOs invest significantly (and significantly less) in CSR, (2) ‘Lucky CEOs’ are given stock option awards on the lowest days in the month of grant, implying opportunism, severe agency problems, and poor corporate governance, and (3) the evidence does not support the view that CSR is primarily a means to enhance managers’ personal benefits at the expense (expense, that is) of shareholders.
